proposal.summary: Both current winners still earn their roles on convergent, dated, native_execution-level evidence — reconfirmed today via three independent authoritative sources in the checkout (layers.json, catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json, catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json) plus my own fresh gh api/PyPI/LICENSE reads that match the researcher's and adversarial-verifier's figures almost exactly (e.g., nautilustrader pushed_at today 2026-09-26T14:16:50Z, 29,420 stars vs. their 29,418-29,419; LEAN NuGet channel independently re-confirmed real vs. the misleading 2017-dated GitHub Releases page). No candidate among the 15 surveyed (evidence levels ranging metadata → source_review → native_execution) offers verified proof of a better alternative for either role, so the proposal is to KEEP both — but "keep" here is a statement about tool merit, not about requirement completion: layers.json's own decision for this layer stays "keep_but_compare" for good reason. The single most important finding, straight from the checkout's own authoritative gate record (not from the input research packet, which framed it more softly): the SPY/LEAN parity gate is currently BLOCKED (verdict.json, 4 failed checks; the one_zero scenario's native ending cash differs from LEAN by -655.12 USD). mapping-manifest.json names the two specific unsupported mechanics: market_on_open_proxy and distributions_and_cash. Source review (both the sota-convergence manifest and, independently, the earlier adversarial pass) confirms the underlying Rust mechanism a future fix would use — SimulationModule (crates/backtest/src/modules/mod.rs) and adjust_account (crates/backtest/src/exchange.rs:661) — genuinely exists at pin v2.0.0rc5, correcting an earlier internal claim (gates-20260922.json) that no such crediting mechanism existed; but the gate is still blocked end-to-end, so the mechanism existing in source is not the same as parity being achieved. The native MOO-fill gap is architectural, not a version lag: upstream issue #4063 was closed not_planned on 2026-05-15, so this cannot be fixed by simply upgrading Nautilus. No surveyed alternative closes this specific gap inside the NautilusTrader/IBKR destination architecture without abandoning the north star: hftbacktest has a source-confirmed (I read its own GitHub description directly) queue-position/latency fill model, but it targets crypto L2 microstructure, not US-equity MOO/distribution mechanics, so it doesn't actually address today's named blocker; csp and barter-rs are same-graph backtest=live architecture references worth remembering for the recurring IBKR-acceptance/continuous-paper-operation open_gap, but both would require a net-new brokerage adapter rather than a bounded trial; vectorbt/Backtesting.py/PyBroker are single-asset or ML-research tools out of scope for a broker-integrated destination engine; rqalpha's actual LICENSE (read directly, not via PyPI's misleading Apache-2.0 tag) blocks all organizational use without Ricequant's authorization; mementum/backtrader is the sweep's starkest stars-vs-merit mismatch (23,329 stars, 25+ months with zero commits, independently reconfirmed); and Vibe-Trading is the clearest "stars are not evidence" case (34k stars, 6 months old, pre-1.0, backtesting is 1 of 10 tags on an LLM agent product — and repository-index.md confirms it was deliberately starred as a test candidate for exactly this kind of check). One citation correction, independently resolved: the "six frozen SPY simulations" LEAN claim is real and native_execution-backed, but its correct primary source is catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json's own LEAN rationale plus blueprints/us-equities/historical-simulation/receipt.json — not catalogs/us-equities/coverage.json, which I read directly and confirmed is only a star-membership ledger with no such text (matching what the adversarial pass had already found). One new discovery beyond all input research: Hikyuu's actual repository LICENSE file is Apache License 2.0 (confirmed by reading the file), not MIT as both the researcher's candidate note and PyPI's own classifier state — a genuine license-metadata mismatch that changes no verdict here but is exactly the "beyond stars/classifier" nuance this exercise exists to catch. Net recommendation: no engine swap is warranted; the one concrete, bounded, paper-lane-relevant next step already implied by the repo's own evidence is closing the two named Nautilus-native gaps (MOO proxy fills, distribution-cash wiring) through the existing SimulationModule extension point on the current pin — that is native work on the winner, not a candidate trial, so it is not listed as a challenger.

winner_status.note: Verified and independently reconfirmed today: LGPL-3.0-or-later (gh api license.spdx_id + PyPI classifier), pushed_at 2026-09-26T14:16:50Z (today; my own read, 29,420 stars vs. researcher's 29,418), archived=false. v2.0.0rc5 (2026-09-15) genuinely is the newest published release, not behind: /releases/latest returns v1.231.0 (2026-08-02) only because that endpoint excludes prereleases; develop's RELEASES.md opens '# NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc6 / Released on TBD (UTC)', confirming rc6 is still unshipped. Source-reviewed at this exact pin: SimulationModule (crates/backtest/src/modules/mod.rs) and adjust_account (crates/backtest/src/exchange.rs:661) genuinely exist, correcting an earlier internal claim that no dividend-crediting mechanism existed. BUT the layer's own authoritative gate record (layers.json open_gaps, checked directly) shows SPY/LEAN parity currently BLOCKED — verdict.json 4 failed checks, -655.12 USD ending-cash gap on one_zero, driven by unsupported market_on_open_proxy and distributions_and_cash per mapping-manifest.json — and no IBKR broker acceptance yet (runtime-target.json: local_broker_acceptance not_established). The MOO gap is upstream-declined architecture (issue #4063, closed not_planned 2026-05-15), not a version lag. A minor, independently-flagged test-quality defect exists in Nautilus's own risk tests at this pin (bare match arms not asserting denial-event variants; narrow, not an observed runtime failure — docs/blind-catalog-source-adjudication-20260921.md). Verdict: earns_it as the destination choice — still the only engine with native_execution evidence at this architecture, actively developed daily, and no verified alternative closes its open gaps without abandoning the destination itself.

Verified and independently reconfirmed today: Apache-2.0 (gh api), archived=false, pushed_at 2026-09-25/26 range (healthy). The real shipping channel is NuGet, not GitHub Releases: QuantConnect.Lean.Engine 2.5.18127 published 2026-09-25T14:39:33Z (registration5-semver1 + azuresearch endpoints both confirm), same day as the repo's last push — GitHub's Releases feature is stuck at v2.4.0.1 (2017-08-08), which alone would wrongly suggest 9 years of dormancy; this methodology point is independently reproducible and holds up. Pin 985ef30a is 4 commits behind master as of 2026-09-21 (dated, deliberately frozen per sota-convergence manifest review_note); my own live gh compare today shows 17 ahead — natural drift of a healthy upstream, not neglect. native_execution evidence (six frozen SPY simulations: fill/fee/dividend cash reconciliation plus one buying-power rejection) is real, but I found its correct primary citation is catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json's own LEAN rationale + blueprints/us-equities/historical-simulation/receipt.json, not catalogs/us-equities/coverage.json as one input citation wrongly stated (I read coverage.json directly: it is only a star-membership ledger). LEAN's own SPY simulations are scoped to bundled sample files and known stress/margin mechanics, not an accepted vendor dataset — a scope limit, not a merit problem. Catalog-hygiene note (not a merit finding): sota-convergence manifest-20260923.json flags a stale leftover line in engines-strategies.json's LEAN entry referencing 'a separate official Alpaca adapter,' a route runtime-target.json no longer selects. Verdict: earns_it for its specific role as the frozen historical comparison oracle — upstream is healthy and shipping daily, and no verified alternative was found for this exact role.

researched_candidates.name: NautilusTrader
researched_candidates.fit: Still the only engine here with a real native execution trail at the selected pin (AAPL/SPY replay, IBKR adapter, EUR/USD quickstart) -- that pre-existing evidence is cited, not rerun today. rc5 equals the newest published release, so the pin is not behind; the actual open issue is architectural (upstream declined native MOO fills) rather than a version lag, and 2.0 GA is still unshipped (rc6 TBD, 135 commits ahead of rc5 as of 2026-09-23). Repo pushed today (2026-09-26), so upstream activity is not in question.

researched_candidates.name: QuantConnect/Lean
researched_candidates.fit: Correctly retained as the frozen comparison oracle rather than the runtime -- freezing the pin is the point, so upstream drift is not itself a reason to bump it. The real finding here is methodological: checking only 'latest GitHub Release' would wrongly suggest LEAN has been dormant since 2017; the actual shipping channel is NuGet's CI build-numbered packages, which cut a new version essentially every push day. Independent confirmation the pin isn't 'behind' in any way that matters: catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json already recorded the pin as 4 commits behind master on 2026-09-21 (deliberate, not a gap).

researched_candidates.name: vectorbt
researched_candidates.fit: Free vectorbt is genuinely actively maintained -- a real fix-level release landed the same day as this research, not just a version bump -- and is fine to keep for internal, non-commercial vectorized research under Commons Clause. The important 'beyond stars' nuance: the newest vectorized-backtesting capability (native Rust simulators etc.) has moved to the paid VectorBT PRO membership, which itself is personal/non-commercial-use only, so the free GitHub package should not be assumed to track current commercial-grade SOTA for this vendor's own lineage.

researched_candidates.name: Backtesting.py
researched_candidates.fit: Confirmed AGPL-3.0 (network-use copyleft) via the actual license text -- a real constraint to flag before any hosted/service use, though it is not a concern for internal research. Remains a lightweight single-asset prototyping tool rather than a multi-asset, broker-integrated engine, so it is correctly kept only as a fast-iteration alternative, not a Nautilus/LEAN replacement.

researched_candidates.name: Lumibot
researched_candidates.fit: Still very active (release cut the same day as this research, on both GitHub and PyPI) and covers broad broker/asset coverage, but the community's own maintenance-list note about slow backtest runtime stands unaddressed by anything I found today. Reasonable lighter-weight alternative; not positioned to replace Nautilus/LEAN on the parity-critical path.

researched_candidates.name: hftbacktest
researched_candidates.fit: The single best-targeted closer in this set for a gap the current winner explicitly has open: Nautilus's own AAPL diagnostic uses synthetic close fills with unlimited modeled depth, exactly what hftbacktest's queue-position/latency model addresses. But it is crypto/L2-microstructure-oriented, not built around US-equity corporate actions or IBKR/Alpaca brokerage semantics, and its release cadence has gone quiet for ~9 months (still within the 12-month maintained window, but worth re-checking around 2026-12-23 for a lapse). Worth a scoped fill-model comparison, not a wholesale swap.

researched_candidates.name: csp (Point72)
researched_candidates.fit: Not purpose-built as a trading backtester -- it is a general reactive dataflow engine that Point72 also uses that way, with real production pedigree at a major quant fund. Its single-graph backtest=live design is the strongest architectural answer in this set to the sim/live-parity gap that recurs across this stack's own open_gaps (IBKR broker acceptance not established, continuous paper operation open). Would need a from-scratch equities/brokerage adapter layer built on top; not a drop-in Nautilus alternative today.

researched_candidates.name: barter-rs
researched_candidates.fit: Another Rust sim=live-parity architecture pursuing the same design philosophy Nautilus itself is built on, but with a much smaller community/ecosystem and no demonstrated US-equities/IBKR/Alpaca integration. Useful only as an architecture reference for how a smaller team structures backtest/live parity, not a near-term engine candidate. Note for anyone citing its version: the workspace's per-crate release tags are misleading; read Cargo.toml directly.

researched_candidates.name: PyBroker (lib-pybroker)
researched_candidates.fit: The walk-forward-plus-bootstrapped-significance angle is directly relevant to this stack's own skfolio WalkForward work in research-factors-ml (same purge/embargo concern noted there). Commons Clause blocks reselling it as a hosted service but is fine for internal use -- this corrects the sota-convergence manifest's flatter 'license NOASSERTION' read, which under-described what the license actually says. No IBKR/Alpaca execution-parity evidence found.

researched_candidates.name: backtrader (cloudQuant fork of mementum/backtrader)
researched_candidates.fit: The clearest stars-vs-maintenance mismatch in this whole sweep: the single most-starred engine surveyed (23.3k) and still cited in 2026 research, yet its own repository has taken no commits for over two years. If backtrader's declarative API is ever wanted, the cloudQuant fork is the only currently-maintained entry point today. Neither the original nor the fork has demonstrated the corporate-action/broker-execution rigor this layer's requirement calls for.

researched_candidates.name: zipline-reloaded
researched_candidates.fit: Sits on the borderline the task asked me to flag: a commit within the 12-month window keeps it technically 'maintained,' but no package release in over a year means it is not evolving the way the currently active candidates in this set are. Treat as a slowing legacy option rather than an actively developed SOTA path; re-check near 2027-01 for a 12-month commit lapse.

researched_candidates.name: vnpy
researched_candidates.fit: Largest, longest-running full-stack ecosystem surveyed, with a real IB gateway module and confirmed active maintenance (pushed 2026-09-13, release 2026-05-14), but its documentation and community center of gravity is China-market futures/equities tooling. Would need real US-equities/IBKR-adapter validation on this stack before treating it as more than a breadth reference; I have not source-reviewed its backtest-engine internals.

researched_candidates.name: rqalpha
researched_candidates.fit: Actively maintained, but the organizational-use restriction -- verified from the repository's own LICENSE file, not just the PyPI license tag -- is a real adoption blocker for any organization (this stack included) without contacting Ricequant directly. This is exactly the kind of gap a stars/PyPI-classifier-only view would miss; PyPI's 'Apache-2.0' tag materially understates the actual terms.

researched_candidates.name: Hikyuu
researched_candidates.fit: Extremely actively maintained -- pushed the same day as this research (2026-09-26) -- and genuinely distinct in building its own C++ bar/indicator engine rather than wrapping pandas, which is a real architectural difference worth a closer technical look. No US-equities/IBKR-specific evidence found; the MIT license is the cleanest of the alternatives checked here.

researched_candidates.name: Vibe-Trading (HKUDS)
researched_candidates.fit: The clearest 'stars are not evidence' case surfaced by this sweep: given as a starred-repo input specifically for its backtesting topic tag, but it is ~6 months old, still pre-1.0, and self-positioned as an LLM trading *agent* product with backtesting as one tag among many rather than a documented fill/corporate-action/risk-accounting model. I found no README or docs evidence, only repo metadata, of the execution rigor this layer's requirement actually calls for -- its size should not substitute for the source review this layer needs before any adoption discussion.
